description.summary: This Senate resolution honors two Christian County, Missouri deputies killed on February 23, 2026, offers condolences to their families, condemns violence against officers, and affirms support for law enforcement. It names Deputy Gabriel Ramirez and Deputy Michael Hislope, notes four officers were shot (two fatally), and is a nonbinding congressional statement, not a law.

impact.summary: The Senate resolution would formally honor Deputies Gabriel Ramirez and Michael Hislope of the Christian County Sheriff's Office, express condolences to their families for the February 23, 2026 shooting, and recognize Missouri police officers' sacrifice. It also records the Senate's condemnation of violence against law enforcement and expresses support for law enforcement nationwide without creating legal obligations.

The resolution would void the EPA rule (90 Fed. Reg. 55671) that extended deadlines in the Oil and Natural Gas Sector climate review, removing the agency's extension. This affects EPA enforcement and oil and gas operators (wells, pipelines, compressor stations, processing plants) and the state air agencies that implement Clean Air Act NSPS and Emissions Guidelines.

description.summary: This joint resolution, under the Congressional Review Act, disapproves and voids the EPA rule (90 Fed. Reg. 55671, Dec. 3, 2025) that extended deadlines in Standards of Performance and Emissions Guidelines for the oil and natural gas sector. If enacted, it would remove nationwide those deadline extensions for new, reconstructed, modified, and existing sources, affecting owners and operators of oil and gas facilities.

This bill amends the Illegal Immigration Reform and Immigrant Responsibility Act to require 501(c)(3) nonprofits that pay individuals for political services or to take an active part in political management or campaigns to enroll in and comply with the federal E‑Verify program. It applies nationwide to tax‑exempt public charities and covers paid (not volunteer) workers, obligating organizations to use E‑Verify to confirm workers' authorization to work in the United States.

impact.summary: The bill requires 501(c)(3) tax‑exempt nonprofits that pay people to do political work or take active roles in political campaigns to enroll in and follow the federal E‑Verify program. It would affect charities and community groups nationwide and the Department of Homeland Security/USCIS, which operates E‑Verify.

description.summary: This bill amends the Radiation Exposure Compensation Act to add Guam as a covered Pacific test area, add renal disease to compensable illnesses, set specific qualifying presence periods for leukemia and other listed diseases, and include Enewetak Atoll radiological‑cleanup personnel. It applies to individuals physically present in affected Pacific areas during the listed dates (including the 1946–1992 windows and April–November 1962) and to Armed Forces who cleaned up Enewetak (May 1, 1977–May 31, 1980).

impact.summary: The bill adds Guam to the Radiation Exposure Compensation Act’s list of Pacific test sites, extends covered exposure dates, and adds Enewetak Atoll radiological‑cleanup participants (May 1, 1977–May 31, 1980). Guam residents and U.S. Armed Forces veterans from that cleanup could file leukemia and specified‑disease claims, now including renal disease, with the Justice Department’s Radiation Exposure Compensation Program.

description.summary: The bill creates a Commerce Department task force to research and recommend starting antidumping, countervailing duty, and circumvention investigations. It directs the task force to monitor trade flows, pricing, foreign subsidies, consult other agencies and U.S. industries, prioritize impacts on small and medium-sized U.S. firms, and keep findings confidential until formal initiation under sections 702(a), 732(a), or 781 of the Tariff Act.

impact.summary: Creates a Commerce task force under Under Secretary for International Trade to flag countervailable subsidies, dumping, and circumvention and to recommend starting investigations under the Tariff Act. It will consult the U.S. International Trade Commission and Customs and Border Protection, monitor imports and foreign subsidies, prioritize harms to small and medium-sized U.S. businesses, and keep findings confidential until investigations open.

description.summary: The bill requires U.S. Customs and Border Protection to refund, with interest, all duties imposed under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act to each importer of a covered article and to reliquidate previously liquidated entries, with refunds due within 180 days. CBP must prioritize small businesses, coordinate Small Business Administration outreach, send 30-day reports to finance and small business committees, and issue drawback guidance in 60 days.

impact.summary: The CBP Commissioner must refund, with interest, all duties collected under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act to importers of covered articles, reliquidate pre-enactment entries, and complete refunds within 180 days. CBP must prioritize small business concerns, coordinate outreach with the Small Business Administration, issue drawback guidance under the Tariff Act (19 U.S.C. 1313), and report monthly to congressional finance and small-business committees.

description.summary: The bill requires foreign payment stablecoin issuers with over $50 billion in consolidated issuance and not subject to SEC Section 13(a) or 15(d) reporting to prepare GAAP annual financial statements that disclose related‑party transactions and to obtain annual audits conducted under PCAOB auditing standards by registered auditors. It amends section 18 of the GENIUS Act and clarifies this requirement does not alter PCAOB jurisdiction over permitted payment stablecoin issuers or auditors.

impact.summary: Foreign payment stablecoin issuers with over $50,000,000,000 in consolidated outstanding issuance that do not file SEC reports under sections 13(a) or 15(d) must prepare GAAP annual financial statements disclosing related‑party transactions. They must engage a registered public accounting firm to audit those statements under PCAOB auditing standards, including auditor independence, internal controls, and related‑party rules.

description.summary: The bill directs FEMA, within 120 days, to revise 44 C.F.R. §206.48 to apply fixed weighted criteria for Public Assistance (10/40/10/10/10/10/10: cost; localized impacts; insurance; mitigation; recent disasters; other Federal aid; economic) and Individual Assistance (20/20/20/10/20/5/5: concentration; trauma; special populations; voluntary agencies; insurance; state average aid; economic). It applies to Governors’ requests for Stafford Act major disaster declarations denied on or after January 1, 2012.

impact.summary: FEMA's Administrator must amend 44 C.F.R. §206.48 within 120 days to assign weights when evaluating Public Assistance (localized impacts 40%, cost 10%) and Individual Assistance (damage concentration 20%, trauma 20%, insurance 20%). The change alters how FEMA decides Governors' Stafford Act requests and affects states, localities, survivors, voluntary agencies, and insurers for disasters denied on or after January 1, 2012.

description.summary: This bill amends 5 U.S.C. 6103 to set Washington's Birthday on February 22 (instead of the third Monday in February) and to add Lincoln's Birthday to the list of legal public holidays. It revises the federal government's official holiday list under title 5, affecting federal employee leave and federal agency observances.

impact.summary: The bill would amend 5 U.S.C. §6103 to move Washington's Birthday from the third Monday in February to February 22 and to add Lincoln's Birthday as a legal public holiday. That change would alter federal employee leave, pay, and agency closure schedules, affecting executive departments, the U.S. Postal Service, and federal courts; some states and private employers might follow suit.

description.summary: Authorizes the Secretary of the Navy to transfer one or more F‑14 Tomcat aircraft in Navy or DoD custody to the U.S. Space and Rocket Center Commission in Huntsville, AL, by sale, gift, loan, or otherwise under terms the Secretary sets, including demilitarization, indemnification, and limits on further disposition. Transfers are at the Commission's expense, and the Commission may hire nonprofits to restore and operate the aircraft for public display, airshows, and commemorations.

impact.summary: The Maverick Act authorizes the Secretary of the Navy to transfer F-14 Tomcat aircraft from Department of the Navy or Department of Defense custody to the U.S. Space and Rocket Center Commission in Huntsville, Alabama. The Commission would bear all transfer, restoration, operation, and maintenance costs, may face demilitarization or indemnification requirements, and may partner with nonprofits to display jets at museums, airshows, and commemorations.

description.summary: The American Homeownership Act disallows federal income tax deductions for interest paid on residential rental property when an institutional investment entity or a "large owner" holds a majority interest. It covers single‑family rentals aggregated at 50+ units and institutional investment vehicles, and creates exceptions for sales to individuals or qualified nonprofits, certain new construction and rehabilitation, federally assisted and low‑income housing, and multi‑family properties.

impact.summary: The bill bars federal tax interest and depreciation deductions for residential rental properties majority‑owned by institutional investment entities (for example, 3(c) private funds) or by “large owners” holding 50+ single‑family rental units. Exemptions apply to sales to individuals or qualified nonprofits (community land trusts, public‑housing agency subsidiaries), new construction after 2023, rehab of uninhabitable units, and HUD‑assisted or LIHTC properties.

description.summary: The bill amends 38 U.S.C. 8127(h) to remove paragraph (3), renumber paragraph (4) as paragraph (3), and insert the phrase "established under the Small Business Act (15 U.S.C. 631 et seq.)" into the redesignated paragraph. The change applies to the Department of Veterans Affairs' procurement preference hierarchy, clarifying that the referenced small-business preference covers entities established under the Small Business Act for VA contracting.

impact.summary: The bill amends 38 U.S.C. 8127(h) to require the Department of Veterans Affairs' procurement hierarchy to use small‑business categories "established under the Small Business Act." It would affect VA contracting offices and firms bidding on VA contracts—especially veterans‑owned and service‑disabled veteran‑owned small businesses and other Small Business Administration–defined small business categories—by aligning VA preferences with SBA definitions.

description.summary: The bill amends the Elizabeth Dole 21st Century Veterans Healthcare and Benefits Improvement Act to extend VA burial benefits through 2030 for veterans who die at home while receiving VA‑furnished hospice care. It does so by changing the expiration year in section 301(c)(2) (38 U.S.C. 2303 note) from 2026 to 2030.

impact.summary: This bill extends from 2026 to 2030 a provision that lets veterans who die at home while receiving VA‑furnished hospice care remain eligible for Department of Veterans Affairs burial benefits. It affects those veterans and their survivors who claim burial allowances and the VA offices that pay or provide those benefits, including the Veterans Health Administration and National Cemetery Administration.

description.summary: The bill directs USDA Rural Development to reserve at least 2.5% of appropriated funds per discretionary grant program to provide technical and predevelopment assistance so low‑capacity rural communities can prepare and implement projects. Supports training, environmental review, outreach, and application development for broadband, water/wastewater, housing, and community projects; prioritizes persistent‑poverty, underserved, or low‑capacity areas and eligible local, Tribal, nonprofit, cooperative, extension, college, or private entities.

impact.summary: The bill requires USDA to reserve at least 2.5% of funds for Rural Development grants for technical assistance, pre‑development, outreach, and application support for broadband, water/wastewater, housing, and community projects. USDA Rural Development (RUS, RBCS, RHS) and State offices would fund technical‑assistance providers—local and Tribal governments, nonprofits, co‑ops, land‑grant colleges, and private firms—for low‑capacity and persistent‑poverty rural areas.

description.summary: The bill permanently establishes an Emergency Safety and Security Grant Program in the U.S. Housing Act of 1937, authorizes $225 million annually, and directs HUD to award grants to public housing agencies for purchase, installation, repair, or replacement of security and safety items. Eligible items include cameras, fencing, lighting, alarms, locks, CO/smoke detectors, and heating fixes; per‑agency cap $250,000 (exceptions for extra‑large or >5,000 units).

impact.summary: The bill requires HUD to make permanent an Emergency Safety and Security Grant program, authorizes $225 million yearly plus a Capital Fund set‑aside, and awards grants to public housing agencies (PHAs). Grants fund security and safety items—cameras, lighting, locks, CO/smoke detectors, heating fixes—with a $250,000 cap per PHA unless extra‑large or >5,000 units, affecting HUD, PHAs, residents, and contractors.

description.summary: The bill extends the Export‑Import Bank's statutory authorization by changing its termination date from 2026 to 2036 and extending the Bank's aggregate loan, guarantee, and insurance authority expiration from 2027 to 2037. It also renews the "China and Transformational Exports" program authorization through 2036, preserving Ex‑Im's authority to provide loans, guarantees, and export‑credit insurance to support U.S. exporters.

impact.summary: The bill extends the Export-Import Bank of the United States’ charter and its loan, guarantee, and insurance authority by ten years (from 2026/2027 to 2036/2037). It keeps the EXIM China and Transformational Exports program active and affects U.S. exporters and manufacturers (for example aerospace, heavy equipment, and clean-energy firms) plus their foreign buyers who use EXIM financing.

description.summary: The bill creates a Department of Education pilot to award competitive grants—up to $200,000 for two years, with $10 million authorized for FY2026—for buying, distributing, or donating books and hosting literacy programs and other book‑access activities. Grants cover nongovernmental and nonprofit groups serving children under 19, require a community leader letter and viewpoint‑neutral review, include report to Congress, and do not compel libraries to accept donations.

impact.summary: The bill directs the Department of Education to run a competitive pilot awarding nonprofit or nongovernmental organizations grants (up to $200,000; $10 million authorized for FY2026) to provide books and literacy programs for children under 19. It requires viewpoint-neutral review, lets libraries refuse donations, and directs the Secretary to report to Congress on books distributed and child literacy changes.

description.summary: The BO's Act directs HHS to study and report to Congress within one year on home cardiorespiratory monitors for infants and their role in preventing sudden unexpected infant death. The report must assess device accuracy and effectiveness—especially for high‑risk infants—outline care models using monitors, set medical‑coverage criteria, and recommend whether public or private insurers should cover them.

impact.summary: The bill directs the Secretary of Health and Human Services to study and report within one year on the effectiveness and accuracy of home infant cardiorespiratory monitors for preventing SUID, focusing on high‑risk infants and home‑sleep care models. It would inform HHS (including CDC), pediatricians and families, monitor manufacturers, and public and private insurers, potentially shaping Medicaid and private coverage.

description.summary: The Affordable CHOICE Act creates a public insurance option under the ACA to be offered by HHS through the Exchanges beginning plan year Jan. 1, 2027, as metal-level (bronze, silver, gold) plans with geographically adjusted premiums to fund benefits and administration. The Secretary must negotiate provider and drug payment rates with fallback to Medicare rates, apply the option nationwide to Exchange enrollees and providers, and prohibit transferring insurance risk to contractors.

impact.summary: The bill directs HHS to create a federal public health insurance option sold only through ACA Exchanges starting January 1, 2027, offering bronze, silver, and gold plans. It would affect Exchange enrollees, private insurers competing on Exchanges, hospitals/clinicians/pharmacies paid at Secretary‑negotiated or Medicare rates, the prescription drug market, and the Treasury via a dedicated account and startup appropriations.

description.summary: The bill requires the President to impose visa sanctions—making them inadmissible and revoking visas—against any foreign person the President finds performed or facilitated "chemical or surgical mutilations" of U.S. minors. It covers WPATH members, licensed physicians, and medical facilities; defines mutilation to include puberty blockers, sex hormones, and surgeries; exempts treatment for disorders of sexual development and detransition care; and allows whistleblower and national-security exceptions.

impact.summary: The bill directs the President and State Department to bar entry and revoke visas for foreign persons—including World Professional Association for Transgender Health (WPATH) members, foreign physicians, and foreign medical institutions—that provide puberty blockers, sex hormones, or gender‑related surgeries to U.S. minors. It requires the State Department to accept public tips, report to Congress within 180 days, and allows UN, whistleblower, and presidential national‑security exceptions.

description.summary: The Unauthorized Spending Accountability Act mandates automatic 302(a) allocation cuts for programs with expired authorizations starting in FY2026: a 10% reduction the first unauthorized year and 15% reductions in the second and third unauthorized years, terminating them on Oct. 1 following the third unauthorized year. It covers programs listed in CBO’s annual expired-and-expiring authorizations report and restores cuts if reauthorized with a sunset no longer than three years.

impact.summary: The bill cuts 302(a) allocations for any program the CBO lists as having an expired authorization: −10% the first unauthorized year and −15% in years two and three. After year three the program terminates October 1, agencies may only close out prior obligations, and Congress can restore funding only by reauthorizing for up to three years.

description.summary: The bill awards a Congressional Gold Medal to Charles "Charlie" Kirk, authorizing two gold medals—one presented to his family and one given to the Smithsonian for public display. It directs the Treasury Secretary to design and strike the medals, permits the U.S. Mint to sell bronze duplicates to cover costs, and charges costs and sale proceeds to the United States Mint Public Enterprise Fund.

impact.summary: The bill directs the Speaker and President pro tempore to award two Congressional Gold Medals honoring Charles "Charlie" Kirk — one to his family and one to the Smithsonian Institution. The Treasury Secretary and United States Mint would strike the medal, may sell bronze duplicates to buyers, and use the U.S. Mint Public Enterprise Fund to cover costs and receive proceeds.

description.summary: This Senate resolution formally condemns use of "congressionally directed spending" and "community project funding" (earmarks) and calls for an immediate, permanent restoration of the ban on such earmarks. As a nonbinding Senate resolution, it expresses the chamber's opposition and urges Congress to stop directing taxpayer dollars to earmarks and to rein in federal overspending, but it does not itself change law or appropriations.

impact.summary: This Senate resolution condemns "community project funding" (earmarks) and urges an immediate permanent ban, targeting Members of Congress and the Senate and House Appropriations Committees. It would cut a congressional route of federal dollars to state and local governments, universities, and contractors and curb congressional inserts into agency appropriations such as Defense and Transportation.

description.summary: This bill renames the Kleptocracy Asset Recovery Rewards Pilot Program as the Kleptocracy Asset Recovery Rewards Program, removes a prior three-year limit, and makes section 9703 expire seven years after enactment. It amends section 9703 and the statutory table of contents and thus affects the federal authority that awards payments for information leading to the recovery of assets stolen by corrupt foreign officials.

impact.summary: The bill renames and extends the Kleptocracy Asset Recovery Rewards Pilot Program, replacing its 3-year limit with a 7-year sunset from enactment. It affects the Department of Justice and Treasury and State Departments that run the program, and people or companies who provide information used to recover assets stolen by foreign officials in U.S. forfeiture or repatriation cases.

description.summary: The bill overhauls U.S. patent law by repealing key America Invents Act sections to restore a first‑to‑invent rule with a one‑year grace period and abolish inter partes/post‑grant review and the Patent Trial and Appeal Board. It reinstates the Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences, narrows ineligible subject matter to natural phenomena and mental processes, limits prior art, presumes irreparable harm for injunctions, and authorizes USPTO fee retention.

impact.summary: The bill restores first-to-invent rules and a one-year filing grace, changing how the USPTO and inventors, startups, universities, and tech and pharmaceutical firms secure patents. It abolishes inter partes and post-grant review and the Patent Trial and Appeal Board, restores a Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences, and shifts patent invalidation disputes to federal courts, affecting generic drug makers.

description.summary: This bill directs the Interior Secretary to award, for seven fiscal years after enactment, a grant to the National Law Enforcement Officers Memorial Fund to support the National Law Enforcement Museum's outreach, education, and officer safety and wellness programs. Funds may pay for memorializing line‑of‑duty deaths, compiling fatality data, exhibits, collections and research, and trainings for Federal, State, local, tribal law enforcement and the public.

impact.summary: The bill directs the Secretary of the Interior to award grants to the National Law Enforcement Officers Memorial Fund to support outreach, public education, and officer safety and wellness programs at the National Law Enforcement Museum for seven fiscal years. It affects the Memorial Fund and the National Law Enforcement Museum in Washington, D.C., and federal, tribal, state, and local law enforcement agencies that use the museum's programs.

description.summary: The bill bars entities tied to the People’s Republic of China from acquiring, leasing, or owning U.S. agricultural land. It also temporarily prohibits such entities from purchasing U.S. residential real estate and requires divestment of existing holdings within one year. Coverage includes corporations and organizations tied to the PRC or Chinese Communist Party, their agents and officers, and applies nationwide including U.S. territories.

impact.summary: The bill prohibits entities tied to the People’s Republic of China or the Chinese Communist Party from acquiring or leasing U.S. agricultural land and forces one‑year divestment, enforced by USDA and DOJ. It also establishes a two‑year ban on covered Chinese purchases of residential real estate, enforces that ban via Commerce and DOJ, and requires USDA to set up a compliance office.

description.summary: The PROTECT Act of 2025 adds controlled‑substance offenses (drug trafficking, unlawful possession, paraphernalia) and specified firearms offenses to special tribal criminal jurisdiction, authorizes tribal courts to obtain warrants for stored electronic communications, and permits incarceration through the Bureau of Prisons Tribal Prisoner Program for convictions under that jurisdiction. It applies to participating Indian Tribes and their courts in Indian country and covers prosecution, conviction, and sentencing of Indian and non‑Indian defendants, including when neither party is Indian.

impact.summary: The bill lets participating Indian Tribes and tribal courts prosecute controlled‑substance crimes (trafficking, possession, paraphernalia) and firearms crimes under special tribal criminal jurisdiction, including some non‑Indian cases. It amends the Stored Communications Act to let Tribal courts issue warrants compelling telecoms and online providers to disclose stored communications and allows Tribal convicts into the Bureau of Prisons Tribal Prisoner Program.

description.summary: The PACE Act makes the Child and Dependent Care Tax Credit fully refundable, raises the credit rate from 35% (previously reducible to 20%) to 50% (not below 35%), and indexes the credit’s dollar limits for inflation. It also raises the employer‑provided dependent care exclusion from $5,000 to $7,500, indexes that amount for inflation, and applies to taxable years beginning after December 31, 2025.

impact.summary: The PACE Act raises the Child and Dependent Care Tax Credit to 50% (minimum 35%), makes it fully refundable, and indexes credit limits for inflation beginning in tax years after 2025. It also increases the employer dependent-care exclusion from $5,000 to $7,500, indexes it, and thereby affects taxpayers who pay for child/dependent care, employers offering dependent-care FSAs, and the IRS.

description.summary: This Senate resolution directs the Secretary of State to submit within 30 days a 502B(c) statement on Ghana's human rights practices prepared with DRL and State Legal Adviser. It seeks details on alleged abuses (arrest/detention, torture, disappearances, killings, trafficking), treatment of non‑Ghanaians sent to Ghana by the U.S., U.S. security‑assistance risks and assurances, detention‑condition analyses, names of persons sent in 2025–26, and 2025–26 U.S.–Ghana meetings.

impact.summary: The resolution directs the Secretary of State, with the State Department’s Assistant Secretary for Democracy, Human Rights, and Labor and the Legal Adviser, to submit a 502B(c) report on Ghana to the Senate Foreign Relations and House Foreign Affairs Committees within 30 days. It must detail abuses and treatment of non‑Ghanaians removed to Ghana by the United States, U.S.–Ghana agreements or payments, security‑assistance risks, and 2025–2026 meetings.

description.summary: The resolution asks the Secretary of State to submit, within 30 days, a 502B(c) report prepared with the DRL bureau and the State Department Legal Adviser on Honduras's human‑rights practices to Congress. It requires detailed information on alleged abuses (arrest, torture, killings, trafficking), treatment of non‑citizens removed to Honduras by the U.S., assessments of U.S. security‑assistance risks, agreements or payments, individuals sent in 2025 and 2026, and 2025–26 meeting summaries.

impact.summary: The resolution directs the Secretary of State, with the Assistant Secretary for DRL and the State Department Legal Adviser, to submit within 30 days to the Senate Foreign Relations and House Foreign Affairs Committees a 502B(c) statement on Honduras's human rights. It must report alleged abuses, treatment of migrants removed by U.S. agencies, security‑assistance risks, agreements, and 2025–2026 meetings.

description.summary: The resolution directs the Secretary of State to submit a section 502B(c) report within 30 days, with DRL and Legal Adviser input, on Equatorial Guinea's human rights practices and related U.S. assessments and actions. It must cover alleged abuses (e.g., torture, arbitrary detention, disappearances, extrajudicial killings, trafficking), treatment of non‑citizens the U.S. removed to Equatorial Guinea, pre‑removal assessments, security‑assistance risks, 2025–2026 transfers, and bilateral meetings.

impact.summary: The resolution orders the Secretary of State to submit a 502B(c) report to the Senate Foreign Relations and House Foreign Affairs Committees on human rights in the Republic of Equatorial Guinea. It seeks details about alleged abuses, treatment of non‑citizens the United States removed there, U.S. security assistance risks, agreements or assurances, persons sent in 2025–2026, and meetings with U.S. officials.

description.summary: The resolution directs the Secretary of State to submit within 30 days a statement, prepared with DRL and the State Department Legal Adviser, reporting on Guatemala’s human‑rights practices. It requests credible information on alleged human‑rights abuses, the treatment of non‑Guatemalans removed to Guatemala, U.S. actions and risk assessments for security assistance, records of 2025–26 removals, related agreements or assurances, and meetings between U.S. and Guatemalan officials.

impact.summary: The resolution directs the Secretary of State, with the State Department’s DRL office and the Office of the Legal Adviser, to submit a 502B(c) human-rights report on Guatemala within 30 days. It seeks details on alleged abuses and prison conditions for non‑Guatemalans the U.S. removed, U.S. security‑assistance risks, assurances or agreements, lists of people sent in 2025–2026, and meetings.

description.summary: The resolution orders the Secretary of State, within 30 days, to submit a 502B(c) statement on Uzbekistan’s human‑rights practices prepared with DRL and the State Department Legal Adviser. It requires information on alleged abuses (arbitrary detention, torture, disappearances, trafficking), treatment of non‑Uzbek nationals removed to Uzbekistan, U.S. actions and assessments (including security assistance, assurances, individuals sent in 2025–26), and summaries of 2025–26 U.S.–Uzbek meetings.

impact.summary: The resolution directs the Secretary of State, with the State Department DRL office and Legal Adviser, to deliver a 502B report on Uzbekistan to the Senate Foreign Relations and House Foreign Affairs Committees within 30 days. The report must list alleged Uzbek abuses, U.S. security‑assistance risks, people the U.S. sent in 2025–2026, related assurances, and U.S. agencies' actions on removals.

description.summary: This Senate resolution directs the Secretary of State to submit a 30‑day section 502B(c) report, prepared with the State Department’s DRL and Legal Adviser, on Kosovo’s human rights practices. It focuses on alleged abuses against non‑Kosovo citizens the U.S. sent to Kosovo, U.S. assessments of detention conditions and security‑assistance risks, agreements/transfers in 2025–26, and U.S. efforts to prevent or remedy renditions, trafficking, detention, or returns.

impact.summary: The resolution directs the Secretary of State and the Assistant Secretary for Democracy, Human Rights, and Labor to submit under 22 U.S.C. 2304(c) a report to the Senate Foreign Relations and House Foreign Affairs Committees within 30 days. It demands information on Kosovo’s human‑rights record, treatment of non‑Kosovans the U.S. removed (including 2025–2026), U.S. security assistance, agreements, and related meetings.

description.summary: The bill directs the Department of Transportation to engage a university transportation research institute to create and maintain a national infrastructure intelligence tool that integrates public congestion-related data with the Highway Performance Monitoring System. It applies to DOT, State and local DOTs and metropolitan planning organizations; requires datasets such as speed, origin‑destination, crash, asset, commodity, and truck‑parking data, mandates at least annual updates, and authorizes $50 million from the Highway Trust Fund for five years.

impact.summary: The bill directs the U.S. Secretary of Transportation to contract a university research institute to build a national infrastructure intelligence tool linking FHWA’s Highway Performance Monitoring System with speed, origin‑destination, crash, truck‑parking, freight, and asset‑condition data. USDOT, FHWA, State DOTs, MPOs, and freight/trucking interests would use it, and it authorizes $50 million from the Highway Trust Fund for five years.

description.summary: The RECEIPTS Act conditions DoD's transfer and reprogramming authority on the Department obtaining an unqualified audit after FY2028 and imposes Comptroller qualifications if DoD fails that audit by Dec 31, 2028. If audited clean, the Secretary's transfer cap becomes the greater of $10B or 1% of DoD budget; component reprogramming thresholds become $60M (procurement), $30M (research), $45M (O&M), $30M (military personnel); statutory audit-reporting requirements end.

impact.summary: The bill raises transfer and reprogramming thresholds and ends several DoD audit-reporting requirements once the Department of Defense, military departments, Defense Agencies, and Defense Field Activities obtain an unqualified audit after FY2028. If DoD misses a clean FY2028 audit, nominees for Under Secretary (Comptroller) must be CPAs with prior CFO-level experience at a government agency with an unqualified audit.

description.summary: The bill requires NASA to provide any law‑required report or notice it sends to Congress to the Senate Commerce and House Science committees concurrently and within 10 days of any other congressional delivery, and to keep nonpublic items confidential. It also requires NASA to submit copies of any international agreement or nonbinding space instrument to those committees and to congressional foreign‑affairs committees within 15 days.

impact.summary: The bill requires NASA to give required reports, notifications, and budget reprogramming requests to the Senate Commerce Committee and the House Science Committee within 10 days and directs those items be kept confidential. It also requires NASA to provide copies of any international agreement or nonbinding instrument on NASA’s outer‑space activities to Senate Commerce, Senate Foreign Relations, House Science, and House Foreign Affairs within 15 days.

description.summary: The bill amends the FCRA by replacing "active duty military consumer" with "armed forces member consumer" and defining it to include any armed forces member. Changes affect 15 U.S.C. 1681c‑1(k) and 1681t(b)(1)(K), take effect one year after enactment, and extend the FCRA credit-monitoring provisions to all armed forces members.

impact.summary: The bill amends the FCRA to treat any U.S. armed forces member under 10 U.S.C. 101(a) as an "armed forces member consumer" and extend credit monitoring regardless of duty. It affects Equifax, Experian, TransUnion; lenders and furnishers; credit‑monitoring providers; enforcers CFPB, FTC, state attorneys general.

description.summary: This concurrent resolution expresses support for recognizing March 10, 2026, as "Abortion Provider Appreciation Day" to honor abortion providers and staff. It applauds their courage and care, affirms Congress's commitment to their safety and ability to provide care, and highlights impacts of state restrictions on access nationwide.

impact.summary: This concurrent resolution recognizes March 10, 2026, as "Abortion Provider Appreciation Day" for abortion providers and staff at independent clinics, Planned Parenthood centers, hospitals, and private physician offices. It references patients, communities, roughly 20 States with abortion bans, and the FACE Act.

119/hconres/78.title: Expressing support for the recognition of March 10, 2026, as "Abortion Provider Appreciation Day".

description.summary: This House resolution censures Representative Andrew Ogles and requires him to appear in the House well for a public reading of the censure. It also removes him from the House Committee on Homeland Security, applying only to Representative Ogles and his membership on that standing committee.

impact.summary: This resolution would censure Representative Andrew Ogles for publicly making Islamophobic and anti‑immigrant statements and require him to appear in the well of the U.S. House for a public reading of the censure by the Speaker. It removes him from the House Homeland Security Committee.

119/hres/1113.title: Censuring Representative Andrew Ogles and Removing Him from the House Committee on Homeland Security.

description.summary: This resolution authorizes the U.S. Capitol rotunda for the lying in state of seven named Army service members. The President pro tempore, the Speaker, and the Architect of the Capitol will set the date and arrange the ceremonies for those who served in support of Operation Epic Fury.

impact.summary: This resolution authorizes the U.S. Capitol Rotunda to serve for the lying in state of seven named Army service members, including Major Jeffrey R. O'Brien. It directs the President pro tempore, Speaker, and Architect of the Capitol to set the date and arrange the event.

119/hconres/77.title: Authorizing the use of the rotunda of the Capitol for the lying in state of the remains of Army Major Jeffrey R. O'Brien, Captain Cody A. Khork, Chief Warrant Officer 3 Robert M. Marzan, Sergeant First Class Noah L. Tietjens, Sergeant First Class Nicole M. Amor, Sergeant Declan J. Coady, and Sergeant Benjamin N. Pennington.

description.summary: This House resolution recognizes the 245th anniversary of the Battle of Guilford Courthouse, honors the patriots who fought there, and encourages all United States citizens to visit the Guilford Courthouse National Military Park. It covers the Guilford Courthouse National Military Park in Guilford County, North Carolina, and is nonbinding.

impact.summary: The resolution recognizes the 245th anniversary of the Battle of Guilford Courthouse and honors the patriots who fought there. It encourages U.S. citizens to visit the Guilford Courthouse National Military Park in Guilford County, North Carolina, and affects the National Park Service and local tourism.

119/hres/1111.title: Recognizing the 245th anniversary of the Battle of Guilford Courthouse and encouraging all United States citizens to visit the Guilford Courthouse National Military Park in Guilford County, North Carolina.

description.summary: This Senate resolution supports designating February 21–28, 2026, as "National FFA Week," recognizes the National FFA Organization's role in developing student leaders, and celebrates the 50th anniversary of Alaska's State FFA Association. The nonbinding measure covers the FFA's roughly 1,000,000 members in 9,407 chapters nationwide and specifically notes Alaska's 19 chapters and 493 members.

impact.summary: The Senate resolution designates February 21–28, 2026, as "National FFA Week" and recognizes the National FFA Organization’s role training students for agriculture, food, natural resources, and leadership careers. It notes the FFA’s over 1,000,000 members in 9,407 chapters, about 13,000 advisors and teachers, and celebrates Alaska’s State FFA Association’s 50th anniversary with 19 chapters and 493 members.

119/sres/622.title: A resolution expressing support for the designation of February 21 through February 28, 2026, as "National FFA Week", recognizing the important role of the National FFA Organization in developing the next generation of globally conscious leaders who will change the world, and celebrating the 50th anniversary of the chartering of the State of Alaska as a State FFA  Association.

description.summary: This Senate resolution designates October 5–11, 2025, as "National 4‑H Week" and formally recognizes 4‑H as the youth development program of the Cooperative Extension System and USDA's National Institute of Food and Agriculture. It highlights 4‑H's nationwide reach—about 6 million youth and networks of land‑grant universities, volunteers, and extension professionals in all 50 states—and is a non‑binding resolution that does not change law or funding.

impact.summary: The Senate resolution designates October 5–11, 2025, as National 4‑H Week and recognizes 4‑H as the youth program of the Cooperative Extension System and USDA's National Institute of Food and Agriculture. It spotlights 6 million 4‑H members, nearly 500,000 volunteers, 3,500 extension staff, more than 110 land‑grant universities and National 4‑H Council across all 50 states without added funding.

119/sres/434.title: A resolution expressing support for the designation of October 5 through October 11, 2025, as "National 4-H Week".

description.summary: The resolution urges DOJ and DHS agents reassigned from counterterrorism, cybersecurity, or counterintelligence to civil immigration enforcement be returned to core missions during active hostilities with Iran. It covers those on temporary duty, detail, or reassignment, full- or part-time, since 1/20/2025 and applies to other state sponsors of terror.

impact.summary: The resolution urges DOJ and DHS law enforcement staff reassigned to civil immigration enforcement since January 20, 2025, be returned to missions. Core missions include FBI counterterrorism, HSI, CISA cybersecurity, and DHS intelligence work during active hostility with Iran and other state sponsors of terror.

119/sres/638.title: A resolution expressing the sense of the Senate that the law enforcement agents and other personnel of the Department of Justice and the Department of Homeland Security, who have been temporarily engaging in civil immigration enforcement operations, should be returned to their primary missions during periods of active hostility with Iran.

description.summary: The resolution directs the Senate Committee on Rules and Administration to establish an annual academic civics competition, promulgate necessary regulations, and permit partnerships with public or nonprofit organizations and acceptance of private donations to offset costs. It applies to secondary school students as defined in ESEA section 8101.

impact.summary: The Senate Committee on Rules and Administration would establish an annual academic civics competition for secondary school students nationwide. The Committee may partner with iCivics or the National Constitution Center, accept private donations, and issue regulations for judging and operations.

119/sres/639.title: A resolution establishing an annual Senate academic civics competition for secondary school students.

description.summary: The resolution designates March 10, 2026, as "Abortion Provider Appreciation Day" and expresses support for abortion providers and their staff. It applies nationwide, lauds host communities, affirms Congress's commitment to provider safety and patient access, and condemns actions that restrict or stigmatize abortion care.

impact.summary: The concurrent resolution recognizes March 10, 2026, as "Abortion Provider Appreciation Day" to celebrate abortion providers and staff at independent clinics, Planned Parenthood health centers, hospitals, and private physician offices. It cites 20 States with bans and asks Congress to affirm provider safety and access.

119/sconres/28.title: A concurrent resolution expressing support for the recognition of March 10, 2026, as "Abortion Provider Appreciation Day".

description.summary: The bill requires eventual notice to targets, forbids indefinite sealing, and limits nondisclosure to an initial 180‑day period plus one 180‑day extension with stricter review thereafter. It applies to federal, State, Tribal, and military orders including wiretaps, pen registers, mobile tracking, Section 2705 nondisclosure, search warrants, third‑party assistance, inventories.

impact.summary: The bill stops indefinite sealing and requires eventual notice to targets of criminal-surveillance orders while limiting nondisclosure to providers with 180‑day seals and fewer extensions. It affects federal, State, and Tribal courts, the DOJ and local law enforcement, telecom and tech providers, and surveillance targets.

description.summary: The Keep It Moving Act imposes deadlines on FCC review of transfer or assignment applications, requiring completeness checks within 15 days and final action within 180 days or 1 year on foreign referral, and allows writs compelling action. It applies to all FCC licenses and authorizations for such transfers and assignments.

impact.summary: The bill makes the Federal Communications Commission decide completeness quickly and to approve or deny transfer‑of‑control or license‑assignment applications within fixed deadlines. It affects telecom, broadcast, wireless and cable firms that buy or sell FCC licenses and the Committee for the Assessment of Foreign Participation.

description.summary: The bill requires HUD and the Comptroller General to report to Congress within one year on how many HUD public housing inspections in a year were incomplete. It must also state how many inspectors are needed to ensure all required inspections can be completed annually.

impact.summary: The bill directs the Secretary of Housing and Urban Development and the Comptroller General to study and report how many HUD public housing inspections are incomplete in a year. It affects HUD, the GAO, local public housing authorities, inspection staff, and HUD public housing residents.

119/hr/7700.title: Annual Public Housing Inspections Accountability Act

description.summary: The bill creates a new Title 18 chapter that prohibits indefinite sealing of criminal surveillance orders, requires eventual notice to targets, and tightens nondisclosure and extension standards. It applies to federal, State, Tribal and military orders including wiretaps, pen registers, tracking orders, SCA delay/disclosure orders, search warrants, and related inventories.

impact.summary: The bill bars indefinite sealing of surveillance orders, limits nondisclosure to providers, and requires courts to unseal or redact orders after set periods. It affects DOJ/FBI, federal, state, territorial and Tribal courts, prosecutors, telecom and internet providers, and people targeted by surveillance.

description.summary: This bill amends HEA section 402C(f) to raise FY2027 Upward Bound stipends from $60 to $180, $300 to $900, and $40 to $120, and sets veteran project stipends up to $300. Future maximums will be indexed to the CPI and rounded to the nearest $10 for projects under section 402C.

impact.summary: The bill raises 2027 monthly stipend caps for Upward Bound (TRIO) participants—tripling limits—and allows veterans in subsection (d)(6) projects up to $300. Beginning 2028 the Secretary of Education must annually raise caps by estimated CPI, rounded to $10, affecting Upward Bound grantees (colleges, districts, nonprofits).

119/hr/7690.title: Dr. William W. Sullivan TRIO Upward Bound Student Stipend Support Act

description.summary: This bill adds basic and emergency living-assistance grants to the Student Support Services program to help undergraduate participants cover anticipated or unexpected living and related costs. Recipients may use up to 2% of SSS funds; emergency grants are capped at $500 for 2027–28 and thereafter indexed to CPI increases.

impact.summary: The bill amends the Higher Education Act to require institutions with Student Support Services (SSS/TRIO) grants to provide basic and emergency supplemental living assistance to current SSS participants. It permits 2% of SSS funds for these grants and caps emergency awards at $500 for 2027–28.

119/hr/7689.title: Earl N. Williams, Sr., First Chance Act

description.summary: The bill amends the U.S. Housing Act to set rent in public housing for families with full‑time police officers, firefighters, or emergency medical technicians at the higher of 15% of adjusted monthly income or 5% of monthly income. It applies to units under the Act and to such full‑time public employees.

impact.summary: This bill cuts rents in public housing for families including a full‑time police officer, firefighter, or EMT. Rent becomes the greater of 15% of monthly adjusted income or 5% of monthly income, and public housing agencies verify federal, state, local, or tribal employment.

119/hr/7701.title: Public Housing Rent Reduction for First Responders Act

description.summary: The UASI Act mandates 30% of Urban Areas Security Initiative awards be spent on five National Priority Areas, including minimums of 3% for election security and 10% for ICE‑coordinated border response. It applies to UASI applicants, including State administrative agencies and eligible urban areas, for fiscal year 2027 and thereafter.

impact.summary: This bill would require State administrative agencies and eligible urban areas receiving Urban Areas Security Initiative (UASI) grants to allocate at least 30% of awards across specified National Priority Areas. Also mandates 3% for election security, 10% for border response, ICE cooperation, and grant penalties.

description.summary: The bill lets disabled individuals under early‑retirement age elect to receive SSDI during the five‑month waiting period by writing on applications or appeal filings. Benefits start at 94.25% initially for 36 months with later actuarial adjustments to protect the Disability Insurance Trust Fund and updated SSA forms are required.

impact.summary: The bill lets SSDI applicants elect benefits during the five‑month waiting period and requires SSA to add an election option to applications. It sets 94.25% for 36 months and requires Chief Actuary and Commissioner reviews of effects on the Federal Disability Insurance Trust Fund.

description.summary: The bill bars jurisdictions that prohibit immigration-status data sharing or refuse DHS detainers from receiving SEAR funds and reallocates those funds to ICE. It defines "sanctuary jurisdictions," triggers ineligibility after 30 days unless compliance is certified, prioritizes deportations and border removals, and requires semiannual DHS reports.

impact.summary: The bill bars DHS Special Event Assessment Rating (SEAR) support and Homeland Security Grant Program funds for events in "sanctuary jurisdictions." Savings must go to ICE Enforcement and Removal Operations to prioritize arrests, detentions, and removals, with at least half for border-related enforcement.

119/s/3921.title: Sanctuary Jurisdiction Event Security Enhancement Act

description.summary: This bill exempts "traditional large and premium cigars" from FDA tobacco authority and forbids FDA rulemaking on them (except section 907(d)(3)). Cigars wrapped and filled with 100% leaf tobacco, no filter, tip, or non‑tobacco mouthpiece, weigh ≥6 pounds per 1,000, meet specified binder/manufacture criteria; definition excludes cigarettes and little cigars.

impact.summary: The bill exempts defined "traditional large and premium cigars" from most FDA regulation under the FD&C Act. That change would affect the FDA and the premium cigar industry, including manufacturers, importers, retailers, distributors, tobacconists, and small businesses, by removing regulatory requirements and some user fees.

119/s/3922.title: Traditional Cigar Manufacturing and Small Business Jobs Preservation Act of 2026

description.summary: The bill appropriates "such amounts as may be necessary" to fund Department of Homeland Security administrative expenses during any FY2026 lapse in appropriations and directs DHS to continue all functions and respond to congressional communications during the lapse. It covers DHS generally, including its Office of Legislative Affairs and ICE’s Office of Congressional Relations.

impact.summary: The bill would fund DHS during any FY2026 appropriations lapse, including the DHS Office of Legislative Affairs and ICE’s Office of Congressional Relations. It requires the Secretary to keep DHS performing functions such as border security and disaster response and to respond to congressional offices.

119/hr/7617.title: To provide funding for administrative expenses of the Department of Homeland Security during any lapse in appropriations during fiscal year 2026, to require that the Department be responsive to congressional offices during such a lapse in appropriations, and for other purposes.

description.summary: This resolution orders consideration of H.J. Res. 143, waives points of order, deems a Rules Committee minority substitute adopted, limits debate to one hour, and allows one motion to recommit. It applies to House floor procedure for that joint resolution, suspends rules XIX(1)(c) and XX(8), and requires Clerk to notify Senate in three days.

impact.summary: H. Res. 1068 forces immediate House consideration of H.J. Res. 143, waiving points of order and limiting debate to one hour. It deems a Rules Committee minority amendment adopted, allows one motion to recommit, and impacts House members, leadership, the Clerk, and the Senate.

119/hres/1068.title: Providing for consideration of the joint resolution (H.J. Res. 143) enabling Congress to advance important policies.

description.summary: The bill amends the Elementary and Secondary Education Act to have the Secretary of Education produce best practices on secure firearm storage and suicide prevention and to require certain local educational agencies to create and distribute firearm-safety guidance. Guidance must be distributed to students, parents, and other community members.

impact.summary: The bill would require the Education Secretary to publish firearm secure‑storage and suicide‑prevention best practices and have covered school districts distribute guidance to students, parents, and communities. It requires consultation with ATF, HHS (CDC, NIH, SAMHSA), FBI, law enforcement, non‑industry nonprofits, educators, and mental‑health professionals.

119/hr/7591.title: Secure Firearm Storage and Suicide Prevention Act of 2026

description.summary: This House resolution orders immediate consideration of H.R. 6856, deems a printed substitute adopted, waives points of order, and limits debate to one hour. H.R. 6856 would impose sanctions on the Russian Federation if it refuses to negotiate, breaches a peace agreement, or launches another invasion of Ukraine.

impact.summary: This resolution brings H.R. 6856 to the House floor immediately, waives points of order, deems a Fitzpatrick substitute adopted, and limits debate to one hour. It affects House members and the Rules Committee and enables consideration of sanctions on the Russian Federation related to Ukraine.

119/hres/1067.title: Providing for consideration of the bill (H.R. 6856) to impose sanctions and other measures with respect to the Russian Federation if the Government of the Russian Federation refuses to negotiate a peace agreement with Ukraine, violates any such agreement, or initiates another military invasion of Ukraine, and for other purposes.

description.summary: The SAFE Olympic Sports Act would change Title 36 to require national governing bodies to limit athlete participation to events matching an athlete’s biological sex as defined at conception. It covers Olympic, Paralympic, Pan‑American, Parapan‑American and other national, regional, State, local sanctioned competitions, preserving prior single‑sex event sanctions.

impact.summary: The SAFE Olympic Sports Act would require national governing bodies under Title 36 to limit Olympic‑movement amateur competition by sex, defining sex biologically for Olympic, Paralympic, Pan‑American, and Parapan American events. It also compels NGBs to keep single‑sex competitions they sanctioned in the prior ten years sanctioned.

description.summary: This resolution orders immediate House consideration of H.R. 6636, waives all points of order, deems a specified amendment in the nature of a substitute adopted, treats the bill as read, limits debate to one hour equally divided, and allows one motion to recommit. Applies only to House consideration of HR6636.

impact.summary: This resolution brings H.R. 6636 to the House floor immediately, waives points of order, and deems Rep. Brian Fitzpatrick’s printed substitute adopted. Debate is one hour split between Fitzpatrick and opponent; clause 1(c) of rule XIX is waived and one motion to recommit is allowed.

119/hres/1029.title: Providing for consideration of the bill (H.R. 6636) to advance sensible priorities.

description.summary: The bill lets the President declare an "invasion" at the U.S. southern border and suspend entry and remove aliens who unlawfully cross the border. It bars them from asylum and other relief, requires pre-entry health and security information or removal, and bars judicial review except for U.S. nationality claims.

impact.summary: President may proclaim an 'invasion' at the southern border and direct DHS, State, and the AG to repel, detain, expel, and block entrants. Migrants and asylum seekers crossing the southern border would be barred from entry and asylum, immediately removed, and largely denied judicial review.

119/hr/7105.title: Guaranteeing the States Protection Against Invasion Act of 2026

description.summary: The resolution orders immediate consideration of H.R.7007, waives points of order, and deems a timely ranking-minority substitute adopted. Debate is one hour equally divided, one motion to recommit is allowed, clauses of Rules XIX and XX are suspended, and the Clerk must notify the Senate within three days.

impact.summary: The resolution brings H.R.7007 to House floor, waives points of order, deems Rules Committee's ranking minority member substitute adopted, limits debate to one hour split between Majority and Minority Leaders, and allows one motion to recommit. The Clerk must notify the Senate within three days.

119/hres/986.title: Providing for consideration of the bill (H.R. 7007) to govern on behalf of the American people.

description.summary: The resolution orders immediate House consideration of H.R.185, waives points of order, deems a Rules Committee minority substitute amendment adopted, and limits debate to one hour and one motion to recommit. It suspends clauses of Rules XIX and XX and requires passage be sent to the Senate within one day.

impact.summary: The resolution orders immediate House consideration of H.R.185, waives points of order and some House rules, adopts a substitute submitted by the ranking minority member, and limits debate to one hour. It affects House members, the Rules Committee, leadership, the Clerk, and notifies the Senate.

119/hres/910.title: Providing for consideration of the bill (H.R. 185) to advance responsible policies.

description.summary: This Senate resolution supports a National Move Over Law Day and urges national, State, and regional incident management organizations to promote State move over laws. It targets traffic incident management responders and motorists, asking organizations to educate the public to reduce roadside collisions and deaths.

impact.summary: The Senate resolution backs a National Move Over Law Day and urges federal, State, and regional incident‑management groups to promote State move over laws. That outreach targets FHWA, NHTSA, FMCSA, State DOTs, police, fire, EMS, tow‑truck operators, transportation workers, and motorists to protect roadside responders.

119/sres/527.title: A resolution supporting the goals and ideals of a National Move Over Law Day.

description.summary: The bill directs HHS to establish a Lung Cancer Task Force at NIH to study funding, disparities, screening and report to Congress within 180 days. The Secretary appoints members including at least one NCI and one CDC NCCCP representative; it will examine Federal lung cancer research, funding, access, and screening.

impact.summary: HHS must set up a Lung Cancer Task Force at NIH with members from the National Cancer Institute and CDC’s National Comprehensive Cancer Control Program. The task force will assess disparities, federal research funding, and screenings and must report recommendations to Congress within 180 days.

119/hr/6319.title: Benay Taub Lung Cancer Research Act

description.summary: The bill mandates front-of-package FDA-style warnings on sugar-sweetened beverages, products with non-sugar sweeteners, ultra-processed foods, and items high in certain nutrients and restricts child-directed advertising. Coverage includes packaged goods, multi-packs, vending and online sales, with statutory definitions and exemptions for infant formula, milk, 100% juice, medical, and meal-replacement beverages.

impact.summary: The bill directs HHS FDA to require front of package warnings on sugar sweetened beverages, foods with non sugar sweeteners, and ultra processed items, including vending machines and online retailers. It also restricts marketing to children, affecting manufacturers, advertisers, broadcasters and streaming platforms.

description.summary: The bill excludes military retirement and related benefits from federal gross income, making retired or retainer pay and disability or combat related pensions and allowances tax free. It covers members and former members of the Armed Forces and other uniformed services and applies for taxable years beginning after enactment.

impact.summary: The bill excludes from federal gross income all retired and retainer pay plus monthly disability, pay, annuity, or survivor benefits paid under titles 10, 14, 37, or 38 to members and former uniformed services. It affects DoD retirees, Coast Guard, PHS and NOAA commissioned corps.

119/hr/6190.title: Tax Cuts for Veterans Act of 2025

description.summary: This resolution brings H.R.2003 to immediate House consideration; H.R.2003 would amend the Higher Education Act to set federal student loan interest at 2 percent. It waives points of order, deems the bill read, limits debate to one hour equally divided, allows one motion to recommit, and suspends Rule XIX(1)(c).

impact.summary: This resolution brings H.R.2003 to the House floor immediately, waives points of order, limits debate to one hour, and allows one motion to recommit. H.R.2003 would cut student loan interest to 2%, affecting borrowers with Department of Education Direct loans, loan servicers, and the federal budget.

119/hres/883.title: Providing for consideration of the bill (H.R. 2003) to amend the Higher Education Act of 1965 to lower the interest rate on Federal student loans to 2 percent.

description.summary: H. Res. 884 orders immediate consideration of H.R. 6039, waives all points of order, deems a Rules Committee minority-filed substitute adopted, and limits debate to one hour. It allows one motion to recommit, suspends clause 1(c) of rule XIX and clause 8 of rule XX, and directs prompt Senate notification.

impact.summary: This resolution orders immediate floor consideration of H.R. 6039, waives points of order, limits debate to one hour, and treats a Rules minority substitute as adopted. It affects House members, the Committee on Rules, majority and minority leaders (or designees), the Clerk, and the Senate.

119/hres/884.title: Providing for consideration of the bill (H.R. 6039) to advance commonsense priorities.

description.summary: The bill directs DOT to require AM and digital‑AM receivers as standard, easily accessible equipment in new passenger vehicles and allows civil penalties. It covers passenger vehicles manufactured for sale in, imported into, or shipped in interstate commerce to the United States that are produced after the rule's effective date.

impact.summary: The AM Radio for Every Vehicle Act of 2025 requires DOT to issue a rule requiring all new U.S.-market passenger vehicles to include standard, easily accessible AM or digital AM receivers. It authorizes DOT penalties, DOJ enforcement, a GAO study, impacts automakers and AM broadcasters.

119/hr/979.title: AM Radio for Every Vehicle Act of 2025

description.summary: The bill lets prosecution in U.S. district court begin without an Attorney General transfer motion for juveniles aged 16 or older alleged to have committed certain violent federal offenses. It applies to homicide, aggravated assault (111(b)), motor-vehicle theft/carjacking (2119), robbery (1951) involving 924(c), and aggravated sexual abuse (2241) involving 924(c).

impact.summary: The bill lets U.S. prosecutors start federal district prosecutions without an Attorney General transfer motion for juveniles 16+ accused of specified federal violent offenses (18 U.S.C. ch.51; 111(b); 2119; 1951/924(c); 2241/924(c)). This changes how the Department of Justice and federal courts process those juveniles.

119/s/3133.title: Violent Juvenile Offender Accountability Act of 2025

description.summary: The bill defines "cooperative development" and awards maximum points to RCDG applicants that provide a 25% private cash and in‑kind match. It reauthorizes the USDA Rural Cooperative Development Grant program for FY2025–FY2029 and requires USDA and the RCDG interagency working group to analyze research data and submit annual reports to Congress.

impact.summary: The bill reauthorizes the USDA Rural Cooperative Development Grant (RCDG) program through FY2029 and lets USDA favor nonprofits that pledge a 25 percent private match. It requires USDA and the RCDG interagency working group to analyze cooperative research data and submit annual reports to Congress.

119/s/3075.title: Strengthening Rural Cooperatives and Communities Act

description.summary: H.Res.779 brings H.R.1834 to the floor, adopts H.R.5450 as the substitute, and waives all points of order. It limits debate to one hour equally divided for the Appropriations chair and ranking minority member, allows one motion to recommit, and requires the Clerk to notify the Senate within one calendar day.

impact.summary: This resolution orders immediate House consideration of H.R.1834, adopts H.R.5450 as a substitute, and waives points of order. It restricts debate to one hour for Appropriations leaders, permits a motion to recommit, and directs the Clerk to notify the Senate within one day.

119/hres/779.title: Providing for consideration of the bill (H.R. 1834) to advance policy priorities that will break the gridlock.

description.summary: The ReSCUE Oceans Act requires NOAA to establish a Program to advance marine carbon dioxide removal through research, field trials, monitoring, protocols, standards, validation, and reporting. It applies to activities across U.S. marine waters and EEZ and involves States, Tribes, Native Hawaiian entities, Federal agencies, and voluntary carbon markets.

impact.summary: The bill directs NOAA to establish a Program advancing, monitoring, standardizing, and reporting marine carbon dioxide removal, coordinating NSF, NASA, and NIST. It affects coastal States, territories, the National Sea Grant program, Tribal and Native Hawaiian governments, ocean CDR companies, and voluntary carbon markets.

description.summary: The bill lets agencies pay a single lump‑sum relocation payment to federal employees moved in the interest of the Government instead of current subchapter II reimbursements. GSA must issue regulations on calculation, eligibility, disputes, and appeals to the Civilian Board of Contract Appeals.

impact.summary: Federal agencies may pay a one-time lump sum to employees relocated in the interest of the Government instead of 5 U.S.C. chapter 57 reimbursements. GSA must issue rules for lump-sum calculation and dispute handling, and employees may appeal agency decisions to the Civilian Board of Contract Appeals.

description.summary: This resolution orders immediate House consideration of H.R.155, which would require States to allow unaffiliated voters in federal primaries. It prescribes House floor terms, waiving points of order, adopting a printed substitute, limiting debate to one hour equally divided, allowing one motion to recommit, and exempting Rule XIX(1)(c).

impact.summary: This resolution orders immediate consideration of H.R. 155, waives points of order, adopts Fitzpatrick’s substitute, limits debate to one hour, allows one motion to recommit, and suspends clause 1(c) of House Rule XIX. H.R. 155 would require States to let unaffiliated voters join Federal primaries.

119/hres/731.title: Providing for consideration of the bill (H.R. 155) to require States to permit unaffiliated voters to vote in primary elections for Federal office, and for other purposes.

description.summary: This nonbinding Senate resolution declares support for International Women's Day and reaffirms U.S. commitment to advance and empower women and girls worldwide. It highlights gender‑based violence, child marriage, education and economic barriers worldwide and Taliban restrictions in Afghanistan, and is a congressional statement not new law.

impact.summary: S.Res.640 would have the Senate endorse International Women's Day and the U.S. Women, Peace, and Security agenda. It frames U.S. foreign policy and programs affecting women and girls worldwide, naming the State Department, USAID, UN Women, UNICEF, WHO, and Afghan women under Taliban rule.

119/sres/640.title: A resolution supporting the goals of International Women's Day.

description.summary: The End Warehouse Detention Act forbids funds from Public Law 119‑21 being used to buy or contract for warehouses to detain noncitizens. It also bars those funds from repurposing, operating, staffing, or maintaining any ICE or CBP‑owned warehouse for detention.

impact.summary: The bill bars money from Public Law 119-21 (One Big Beautiful Bill Act) being used to buy or lease warehouses to detain noncitizens. It also bars funds from repurposing, staffing, operating, or maintaining any ICE or CBP warehouse, affecting DHS operations and private warehouse owners.

description.summary: Requires DHS’s Office of Detention Oversight to audit ICE facilities and the ICE Director to report results and remediation to four congressional committees within 30 days. Bars new housing of aliens at ICE facilities until audited deficiencies are remediated and the report submitted, covering new facilities and audited existing ones.

impact.summary: The bill forces DHS’s Office of Detention Oversight to audit ICE detention facilities and requires the ICE Director to send findings and remediation to Congressional Homeland Security and Judiciary committees within 30 days. It blocks new detainees at ICE and privately run facilities until remediated.

description.summary: The bill directs Commerce to establish an exclusion process for covered building products from duties above rates in effect on January 19, 2025, with 15‑day rulings for critical products and 60‑day rulings for others. It covers products and inputs used in single‑family and multi‑family housing, and excludes AD/CVD, section‑201 duties.

impact.summary: The bill directs the Commerce Secretary to set an exclusion process letting U.S. homebuilders and suppliers seek removal of tariffs above 1/19/2025 rates on building materials. CBP will administer exclusions and reliquidations; the Secretary must report quarterly to Senate Finance and House Ways and Means.

description.summary: The bill imposes a 15% excise tax on purchases of newly acquired 1–4 unit single‑family residences by qualifying hedge fund taxpayers and adds a 5‑point corporate surtax plus limits on mortgage interest, depreciation, and QBI benefits. It targets pooled‑fund entities with $50M+ AUM, applies after enactment, and excludes 501(c)(3)s, homebuilders, and owner‑occupied, never‑rented homes.

impact.summary: The bill imposes a 15% excise on purchases of 1–4‑unit homes by "hedge fund taxpayers"—pooled‑investor entities (partnerships, corporations, REITs) with $50,000,000+ AUM. It also adds a 5‑point corporate surtax for those corporations and disallows mortgage‑interest, depreciation, and the 199A qualified business income deduction for hedge‑fund landlords.

119/s/3930.title: HOPE (Humans over Private Equity) for Homeownership Act

description.summary: The bill creates a Student Loan Borrower Advocate at the CFPB, an Office for Students and Young Consumers, and requires an MOU with the Department of Education to access ED systems and resolve student loan complaints. It mandates annual reports and prohibits collecting consumers' personally identifiable financial information.

impact.summary: The bill creates a Student Loan Borrower Advocate at the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau to take complaints and publish annual reports. It requires an MOU with the Department of Education and Student Loan Ombudsman and affects borrowers, lenders and servicers, colleges, campus banking providers.

119/hr/7671.title: Students and Young Consumers Empowerment Act

description.summary: The ReSCUE Oceans Act directs NOAA to fund a program to research, monitor, validate marine carbon removal and develop standards and protocols for voluntary carbon credits. It covers U.S. internal and coastal waters, territorial seas, the contiguous zone, and the exclusive economic zone, and requires Tribal and coastal community engagement.

impact.summary: The ReSCUE Oceans Act directs NOAA to create a Program funding research, monitoring, and standards for marine carbon dioxide removal. It would affect coastal States, coastal communities, National Sea Grant, Regional Ocean Partnerships, Indian Tribes, Native Hawaiian organizations, marine‑CDR developers, and voluntary carbon market participants.

description.summary: The bill lets Retired Reserve members under 60 who receive retired pay enroll in regular TRICARE for retirees instead of TRICARE Retired Reserve. It covers Reserve Component members qualified under chapter 1223, takes effect 18 months after enactment, and preserves exceptions tied to 38 U.S.C. 5304 or 5305.

impact.summary: The bill lets Retired Reserve members (National Guard and Reserve) under 60 who are receiving retired pay enroll in regular TRICARE retired-military coverage instead of TRICARE Retired Reserve. It changes eligibility for the Defense Health Agency's TRICARE program and takes effect 18 months after enactment.

119/hr/7667.title: TRICARE Fairness for National Guard and Reserve Retirees Act

description.summary: The bill adds the District of Columbia to the McIntire‑Stennis Cooperative Forestry Act's list of entities eligible for federal forestry research funds. It makes D.C. eligible alongside states, land‑grant institutions, and territories for McIntire‑Stennis formula and competitive grants supporting forestry research and education.

impact.summary: The bill would amend the McIntire‑Stennis Cooperative Forestry Act to add the District of Columbia to the list of jurisdictions eligible for McIntire‑Stennis research grant funds. It would let District government and District forestry or university research programs apply for grants administered by USDA NIFA.

119/hr/7650.title: McIntire-Stennis Act District of Columbia Equality Act

description.summary: The bill lets the Interior Secretary acquire 551.14 acres labeled "Proposed Addition" on a May 2025 map into Mammoth Cave National Park. It makes a $350,000 figure CPI-adjustable, amends section 11 of the 1942 Act, and covers land in Edmonson and Barren Counties, Kentucky.

impact.summary: The bill authorizes Secretary of the Interior and National Park Service to acquire 551.14 acres in Edmonson and Barren Counties, Kentucky, for Mammoth Cave National Park. It makes the $350,000 acquisition cap annually adjusted by the Consumer Price Index from the Bureau of Labor Statistics.

119/hr/3286.title: Mammoth Cave National Park Boundary Adjustment Act of 2025

description.summary: The bill transfers DOL’s veterans employment programs — job counseling/training/placement, federal hiring services, USERRA administration, and homeless veterans reintegration — to the Department of Veterans Affairs effective October 1, 2027. It transfers personnel and assets, requires VA FY2028 budget requests, preserves pending cases, and lets OMB make incidental adjustments.

impact.summary: The bill transfers from DOL to VA, effective Oct 1, 2027, veterans' job counseling/training/placement (ch.41), federal hiring for veterans (§4214), uniformed‑service employment/remeployment rights (ch.43), and homeless veterans reintegration (ch.20). It revises State duties for veterans' employment specialists and requires VA FY2028 budget requests.

119/hr/6861.title: Consolidating Veteran Employment Services for Improved Performance Act

description.summary: The End Veterans Overdose Act of 2026 directs VA to distribute opioid overdose rescue medications, such as naloxone, at VA pharmacies free and without a prescription and to provide usage information. It covers veterans under 38 U.S.C. 1703 and enrolled family caregivers, restricts PII use, and mandates reports to Congress.

impact.summary: This bill requires VA to provide naloxone and other opioid overdose rescue medications free and without prescription at VA pharmacies to covered veterans and caregivers in the VA family caregiver and general caregiver support programs. It restricts personal-data use and mandates reports to Congress.

description.summary: The bill amends 42 U.S.C. 254r(i)(1) to authorize $12.5 million annually for FY2023–2027 and $13.5 million annually for FY2028–2032 for the State Offices of Rural Health program. It applies to grants made under subsection (a), funding State Offices of Rural Health that support rural health services in States and U.S. territories.

impact.summary: The bill reauthorizes the State Offices of Rural Health program and authorizes $12.5 million annually for FY2023–2027 and $13.5 million annually for FY2028–2032. Those grants fund HRSA's State Offices of Rural Health and help state health departments, rural hospitals, clinics, and other rural health providers.

119/hr/7956.title: State Offices of Rural Health Program Reauthorization Act of 2026

description.summary: This bill requires U.S. federal courts and the D.C. courts to excuse individuals who are breastfeeding from jury service upon request. It amends 28 U.S.C. §1866 and D.C. Code §11-1908 to authorize courts or supervising clerks to excuse summoned breastfeeding individuals in federal courts and in the District of Columbia.

impact.summary: This bill excuses breastfeeding people from jury service in U.S. federal courts (28 U.S.C. §1866) and in D.C. courts (D.C. Code §11‑1908). It lets summoned breastfeeding jurors be excused upon request and changes how federal and D.C. courts and their clerks handle jury selection.

119/hr/7946.title: Jury Duty Exemption for Breastfeeding Act of 2026

description.summary: This House resolution commemorates the fifth anniversary of the March 16, 2021 Atlanta spa shootings, condemns xenophobic anti‑Asian rhetoric, and urges restoration and expansion of DOJ hate‑crime grants. It addresses federal hate‑crime reporting and grant programs, online disinformation, AANHPI mental‑health and education supports, and honors victims, families, and communities.

impact.summary: The resolution commemorates the eight Atlanta spa shooting victims and condemns anti-Asian, xenophobic, and anti-immigrant rhetoric.
