It urges DOJ to restore and expand BJA, COVID‑19 Hate Crimes Act, and Jabara‑Heyer NO HATE Act programs and to support community services, online‑hate responses, and AANHPI education.

119/hres/1116.title: Commemorating the 5-year remembrance of the March 16, 2021, shootings in the Atlanta, Georgia, region and denouncing continuing anti-Asian hate, including the resurgence of xenophobic and anti-immigrant rhetoric.

description.summary: This bill bans selling optional vehicle safety features only as bundles with non‑safety options, requiring they be available for separate purchase or included as standard trim with separate price disclosure. It applies to manufacturers and first purchasers under 49 U.S.C. 30102, defines covered ADAS and alert features, and gives FTC and state enforcement.

impact.summary: The bill requires automakers, dealers, and lessors to sell optional safety features like automatic emergency braking, lane keeping, and driver monitoring separately from luxury packages or include them as standard. The Federal Trade Commission enforces it and state attorneys general may sue for penalties.

119/hr/7372.title: Safety is Not For Sale Act

description.summary: The bill requires DOT to amend the automatic emergency braking standard so AEB systems detect and respond to pedestrians, bicyclists, motorcyclists and other vulnerable road users in daylight and low light across skin, clothing, and gear. It applies to passenger motor vehicles made for sale in the United States.

impact.summary: The bill requires the Secretary of Transportation (NHTSA) to amend the Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard for automatic emergency braking so AEB on passenger motor vehicles operates in daylight and low light and detects pedestrians, bicyclists, motorcyclists, wheelchair users, and ATV/tractor riders. It affects automakers.

119/hr/7353.title: Magnus White and Safe Streets for Everyone Act of 2026

description.summary: The SAFE Exit Act directs the Secretary of Transportation to amend FMVSS No. 206 within two years to require power‑independent, easy‑to‑find manual door releases that mechanically disengage electronic latches and labeled performance and emergency‑responder access provisions when vehicle electrical power is lost. It covers new vehicles with electronic door latches.

impact.summary: Mandates DOT (Secretary/NHTSA) to amend FMVSS No.206 within two years to require intuitive, power‑independent manual door releases and emergency responder access when vehicle electrical power is lost. U.S. automakers and motor‑vehicle manufacturers must install these devices on new vehicles and comply with DOT/NHTSA rules.

description.summary: The bill exempts Purple Heart and Medal of Honor recipients from certain passport fees by amending the Passport Act of 1920. It requires the State Department's Consular Affairs office to make a memorandum of understanding with the Defense Department to verify awards and set documentation for eligible applications and renewals.

impact.summary: The bill exempts Purple Heart and Medal of Honor recipients from certain passport fees. It directs the Secretary of State, via the Assistant Secretary for Consular Affairs, to enter an MOU with the Secretary of Defense and DoD to verify service records and set documentation.

119/hr/7398.title: Passports for Purple Hearts and Medals of Honor Act

description.summary: The bill bars the SEC and exchanges from prohibiting or conditioning closed-end funds' investments in private funds or limiting listing or sales because of such investments. It defines private fund by reference to the Investment Advisers Act, covers closed-end companies including BDCs, and preserves fiduciary, valuation, liquidity, and redemption obligations.

impact.summary: The bill bars the SEC from forbidding closed-end investment companies, including business development companies, to invest any or all assets in private funds as defined by the Investment Advisers Act. It prevents national securities exchanges from refusing to list or trade those closed-end company securities.

description.summary: The ACCESS Act of 2026 raises the crowdfunding threshold requiring financial statements reviewed by an independent accountant from $100,000 to $250,000 and lets the SEC raise it to $400,000 on recommendation of the small-business and investor advocates. It covers issuers using the Regulation Crowdfunding exemption and corrects section 4(a)(6) cross-references.

impact.summary: The bill raises the crowdfunding threshold requiring an independent public-accountant review from $100,000 to $250,000 for issuers using Section 4A. It lets the SEC, after recommendations by the Office of the Advocate for Small Business Capital Formation and the Investor Advocate, raise it to $400,000.

description.summary: This resolution impeaches DHS Secretary Kristi Lynn Arnold Noem, alleging obstruction of Congress and breach of public trust for denying Member oversight, withholding FEMA funds, and directing ICE warrantless arrests and raids. If adopted it would formally impeach Noem and send articles to the Senate, targeting her DHS conduct.

impact.summary: The resolution impeaches Kristi Lynn Arnold Noem, Secretary of Homeland Security. It says she blocked oversight of DHS and ICE detention sites, oversaw ICE warrantless arrests and Chicago raids, and directed FEMA to withhold Emergency Food and Shelter and Shelter and Services Program funds.

119/hres/996.title: Impeaching Kristi Lynn Arnold Noem, Secretary of Homeland Security, for high crimes and misdemeanors.

description.summary: The House resolution urges the Secretary of Defense to review 10 U.S.C. §504 to determine whether to authorize enlistment under subsection (b)(2) for aliens holding DACA employment authorization documents. It would cover DACA recipients with DHS-issued work permits seeking to enlist in the U.S. Armed Forces under that enlistment authority.

impact.summary: This resolution urges the Secretary of Defense to review 10 U.S.C. §504 for authorizing enlistment of aliens with DHS DACA EADs. The review would involve the Department of Defense and could affect DACA recipients seeking to join the U.S. Armed Forces.

119/hres/994.title: Expressing the sense of the House of Representatives that the Secretary of Defense should review section 504 of title 10, United States Code, for purposes related to enlisting certain aliens in the Armed Forces.

description.summary: The bill amends the ACA to impose civil penalties ($10k–$50k negligent; up to $200k knowing) and criminal penalties (up to 10 years) on agents and brokers who submit false enrollment information. Federal Exchanges must verify agent-assisted enrollments, document consent, delay commissions until inconsistencies resolve, and regulate marketing organizations.

impact.summary: The bill lets HHS require verification of agent or broker enrollments in Exchange plans and imposes civil and criminal penalties on agents, brokers, and marketing organizations. It affects HHS Exchanges, issuers, agents, and consumers by requiring documentation, delaying commissions, reporting issuer terminations, preventing unauthorized disenrollments.

description.summary: The Stop CMV Act authorizes hospitals and health care entities to screen newborns up to 21 days old for congenital cytomegalovirus and requires state screening standards. It authorizes HRSA and CDC grants, expands NIH research, and tasks the Advisory Committee and state health officers with procedures, reporting, training, and follow‑up.

impact.summary: The Stop CMV Act would let hospitals and other health care entities screen every infant 21 days or younger for congenital cytomegalovirus and require State health officials to adopt approved screening and reporting procedures. HRSA, CDC, NIH would fund grants, data systems, education, research.

description.summary: The Rural Obstetrics Readiness Act establishes HRSA grant programs and a teleconsultation pilot to support obstetric emergency training, equipment, workforce development, transfer protocols, and rapid telehealth consultation. Awards go to rural hospitals, critical access and rural emergency hospitals, consortia, States and Tribes, and facilities lacking obstetric units; it authorizes $5M (2026–2028) and $15M (2026–2029).

impact.summary: The bill requires HHS/HRSA to grant funds for obstetric emergency training, equipment, staffing, and transfer protocols to rural hospitals, critical access hospitals, rural emergency hospitals, and consortia in maternity shortage areas. It also creates an HRSA teleconsultation pilot for States, political subdivisions, and Indian Tribes.

description.summary: The bill requires group health plans and issuers to cover PSA screening without cost‑sharing for high‑risk men 40+. High‑risk includes African‑American men and men with a first‑degree family history or relevant genetic alteration, effective for plan years beginning January 1, 2025.

impact.summary: The bill requires group health plans and insurers to cover PSA screening without cost-sharing for men 40+ at high risk. It affects private insurers, employer-sponsored and self-insured group plans, the USPSTF guidance, and high-risk groups such as African American men and men with family history.

description.summary: The Act funds DOL competitive grants to community colleges, career and technical education centers, and industry partnerships to build immersive technology career pathways using VR/AR/MR for workforce training. Grants run up to five years, prioritize employer-aligned and accessible programs, and require reporting, independent evaluation, and publication of best practices.

impact.summary: The bill tells the Secretary of Labor to fund community colleges, area CTE schools, Tribal colleges, and industry partnerships to build immersive (VR/AR/XR/MR) career-pathway training. Grants prioritize employer-aligned programs serving veterans and people with disabilities, last up to five years, and require DOL reporting.

119/s/2855.title: Immersive Technology for the American Workforce Act of 2025

description.summary: This House resolution designates March as "Multiple System Atrophy Awareness Month" and expresses support for increased public awareness and funding for research toward therapeutics. It concerns a rare, often fatal neurodegenerative disorder affecting tens of thousands in the United States and represents the House's nonbinding endorsement of awareness and research.

impact.summary: This House resolution designates March as "Multiple System Atrophy Awareness Month" and supports research funding for MSA. It signals support for about 25,000–75,000 U.S. patients, their families, researchers and centers like Stanford's MSA Center of Excellence and agencies such as NIH/NINDS.

119/hres/1117.title: Expressing support for the designation of March as "Multiple System Atrophy Awareness Month" to strengthen public awareness of this neurodegenerative disorder.

description.summary: The resolution requests the Secretary of State to submit, within 30 days under section 502B(c), a State Department statement prepared with DRL and the Office of the Legal Adviser on Cameroon's human rights practices. It requires details on violations, treatment of non‑Cameroonians sent to Cameroon, U.S. assurances, and 2025–26 transfers.

impact.summary: Senate requests a 502B(c) report from the Secretary of State on Cameroon's human rights for congressional committees. Prepared with the Assistant Secretary for DRL and State Legal Adviser, it must cover Cameroon government abuses, U.S. removals including 2025–2026 cases, and risks from U.S. security assistance.

119/sres/637.title: A resolution requesting information on the Republic of Cameroon's human rights practices pursuant to section 502B(c) of the Foreign Assistance Act 1961.

description.summary: The POINT Act criminalizes executive "election interference" and forbids using government property, personnel, information systems, or funds to influence, delay, or alter elections. It applies to the President, Vice President, EOP and senior agency officials including AG, FBI and DNI directors and cabinet managers, forbids military or federal deployments except under the Voting Rights Act or for secession/rebellion.

impact.summary: The POINT Act criminalizes federal executive election interference by named officials—President, Vice President, Attorney General, FBI and DNI directors, and cabinet managers—using government property, personnel, systems, or funds. It forbids Armed Forces deployment to affect State elections, lets States sue, and preserves Voting Rights exceptions.

description.summary: The bill requires DHS to verify personal and biometric data and conduct in-person vetting of Afghan evacuees, maintain a vetting database, report quarterly, and permit GAO audits. It applies to noncitizen, non-military evacuees from Afghanistan during the 2021 U.S. evacuation operations and bars unvetted individuals from Federal means-tested benefits, unemployment.

impact.summary: The bill directs DHS to verify personal and biometric data, conduct in‑person vetting, and create a database for non‑citizens evacuated from Afghanistan, including Operation Allies Welcome evacuees, and report to Congress. Evacuees who refuse vetting are barred from unemployment compensation and Federal means‑tested public benefits.

119/hr/7759.title: Afghanistan Vetting and Accountability Act of 2026

description.summary: Reauthorizes USDA’s heirs property relending program to 2031 and funds nonprofit legal and accounting cooperative agreements to resolve ownership and succession of multi‑owner farmland or forestland. Provides $60 million per year for FY2027–2031 (≤3% admin), prioritizes underserved heirs (limited‑resource, socially disadvantaged, veterans), and requires annual public reports to Congress.

impact.summary: The bill reauthorizes heirs property relending and farmland data programs through 2031 and authorizes $60 million annually for USDA cooperative agreements funding nonprofit legal services. It affects underserved heirs with undivided farmland or forest interests, nonprofit legal providers, and USDA programs requiring ownership to enroll.

119/hr/7761.title: Heirs Education and Investment to Resolve Succession of Property Act

description.summary: The Quantum in Practice Act amends the National Quantum Initiative Act to add "modeling, simulation" to the definition of quantum information science and to insert "quantum molecular modeling or simulation" among section 401(b)(3) research priorities. It applies to federal programs implementing the NQI Act.

impact.summary: The bill amends the National Quantum Initiative Act to add modeling and simulation and to include quantum molecular modeling or simulation in the QIS research program. It would guide NSF, NIST, DOE labs, universities, and researchers to research chemical, pharmaceutical, battery, fertilizer, and defense industries.

description.summary: The Kelsey Smith Act requires providers and carriers to promptly disclose available device location data to law enforcement or PSAPs in emergencies. Requests must assert recent 911 contact or reasonable suspicion of imminent danger, include subscriber or next‑of‑kin consent or documented efforts, and be recorded by the agency.

impact.summary: The bill amends 18 U.S.C. 2703 to require providers to promptly give device location to law enforcement or public safety answering points (911 centers) in emergencies. It affects wireless carriers, ISPs, investigative agencies, subscribers and next-of-kin consent procedures, and intersects state disclosure laws.

description.summary: The bill amends the Sherman Act to deem purchases of residential real estate by certain large investors civil Section 1 antitrust violations. It covers REITs, insurers, and investment companies or private funds with ≥$150,000,000 AUM buying single‑family homes, condos, townhouses, or zoned land, with a homebuilder exception and 90‑day delay.

impact.summary: The bill bars purchases of single-family homes, condos, townhouses, or zoned land by covered entities: REITs, insurance companies, and investment companies or private funds with at least $150,000,000 assets under management. DOJ Antitrust Division must prioritize review and enforcement; effective 90 days after enactment.

description.summary: The bill amends Exchange Act §15B to set MSRB membership: a 15‑member (odd‑number) board with a regulated‑representative majority and minimum broker‑dealer, bank, advisor, and public seats. Those rules govern MSRB appointments, terms, interim members, and SEC removal authority, affecting regulation of brokers, dealers, municipal advisors, municipal entities, and investors.

impact.summary: The bill would amend Section 15B to set MSRB membership rules, 15 members, regulated/public quotas, staggered three‑year terms, and SEC appointment and removal authority. It would affect the MSRB, the SEC, municipal securities brokers and dealers (including bank dealers), municipal advisors, issuers/obligated persons, and investors.

119/s/3935.title: Municipal Securities Rulemaking Board Reform Act of 2026

description.summary: The bill criminalizes knowingly transporting a minor across state or foreign lines to obtain puberty blockers, cross‑sex hormones, or gender‑altering surgery, punishable by up to 10 years' imprisonment and civil suits. It also denies federal funds to governments that permit, facilitate, or fail to cooperate with investigations of such transport.

impact.summary: The bill criminalizes knowingly transporting a minor across state lines to obtain puberty blockers, cross‑sex hormones, or surgical sex‑change procedures, affecting parents and medical providers. It also bars federal funds to states or localities that allow such transport or refuse to cooperate with DOJ investigations.

119/hr/7420.title: Stop Gender Trafficking of Minors Act

description.summary: The Clean Competition Act adds a carbon intensity charge to the tax code that levies fees based on facility or national‑industry carbon intensity and requires annual facility reporting of emissions, electricity sourcing, and production quantities. It covers covered entities, eligible facilities, and covered primary goods within defined covered national industries.

impact.summary: The Clean Competition Act creates a carbon‑intensity charge requiring covered entities and eligible facilities to report GHG emissions, electricity use, and output to the Secretary (Treasury), the Administrator (EPA), and the Secretary of Energy. It sets carbon‑intensity formulas affecting U.S. energy‑intensive manufacturers and import classifications.

description.summary: Creates a carbon‑intensity charge in the tax code that taxes emissions per unit by requiring facilities to report GHG emissions, electricity use, and production. Applies to eligible facilities producing covered primary goods and assigns Treasury, EPA, and Energy to calculate intensities, handle petitions, and administer charges, rebates, and carbon clubs.

impact.summary: The Clean Competition Act adds a carbon‑intensity charge and carbon border adjustment to the Internal Revenue Code. It makes U.S. manufacturers (covered entities) of goods like steel, cement, aluminum, and chemicals report emissions and energy data to Treasury, EPA (GHGRP), and Energy for billing.

description.summary: Creates 49 U.S.C. §5308 authorizing formula grants for urban transit operating, planning, security, and safety projects, with operating grants at 80% federal share. Apportionments use reported operating expenses; recipients must maintain non‑Federal spending, cannot convert fixed‑route to third‑party on‑demand, and may reallocate up to 10% of section 5336 funds.

impact.summary: The bill creates §5308 authorizing FTA grants to urbanized areas for transit operating, planning, security, and safety. It sets an 80% federal share for operating aid and requires transit recipients (for example, New York MTA) to certify they will maintain non‑Federal operating and security spending.

description.summary: The bill requires DHS to verify identities and biometrics and to conduct in-person interviews of noncitizens evacuated from Afghanistan between Jan 20, 2021 and Jan 20, 2022. Unvetted evacuees are barred from unemployment and all means-tested federal benefits until vetted, and DHS must provide quarterly reports while GAO audits compliance.

impact.summary: DHS must verify personal and biometric data, conduct in person vetting, and list criminal and benefit records for non United States citizens evacuated from Afghanistan. Noncompliant evacuees would be ineligible for unemployment compensation and Federal means tested programs such as SNAP, Medicaid, and TANF.

119/s/3310.title: Afghanistan Vetting and Accountability Act of 2025

description.summary: The bill creates a tiered Public Service Loan Forgiveness for Federal Direct Loans made after enactment, forgiving 15% increments and full balance after 120 qualifying payments. It covers borrowers employed in certified public service jobs, requires employment certification (including self‑certification), cancels interest on forgiven amounts, and auto‑defers loans during processing.

impact.summary: Bill requires Department of Education to cancel parts of Federal Direct Loans for borrowers in qualifying public service jobs (government and qualifying nonprofits). It cancels 15% after each 24 payments through 96, forgives remaining balance after 120, requires ED certification, cancels interest, and defers loans.

119/hr/6284.title: Strengthening Loan Forgiveness for Public Service Workers Act

description.summary: S.2957 raises the portion of urbanized-area formula grants reserved for small transit‑intensive cities under 49 U.S.C. 5336(h)(3) from 3 percent to 5 percent. It changes allocations for Federal Transit Administration urbanized-area formula funds, increasing federal shares available to qualifying small cities and their transit agencies.

impact.summary: The bill changes 49 U.S.C. §5336(h)(3) to raise the set‑aside for small transit intensive cities from 3% to 5% of formula grants. That change would shift FTA allocations toward local transit agencies in qualifying small urbanized areas and state transportation agencies that receive them.
